speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the Ministry's projection on unemployment for the first quarter of 2017; (b) what is the average waiting time for local and foreign university graduates to get into the workforce under current circumstances; and (c) how is the softer job market impacting on the older people who are in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Nevertheless, amid current global economic conditions and continued economic restructuring, short-term fluctuations in the unemployment rate are expected.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is consistent with the previous three cohorts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: For older residents, both their employment and unemployment rates have moved up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In 2015, over 98% of local employees who wished to continue working were offered re-employment upon reaching the age of 62.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: There was also a corresponding rise in the long-term unemployment rate by 0.2% from 0.8% to 1% over the same two-year period from September 2014 to September 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: So, both the unemployment rate and long-term unemployment rate for local residents have gone up by 0.2%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The Government will continue to provide extra support to encourage the employment of older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: These include the Special Employment Credit (SEC), which is a wage offset of up to 8% of monthly wages for hiring Singaporean workers aged 55 and above and earning not more than $4,000 a month.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: An additional wage offset of up to 3% is provided for those aged 65 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: From 1 July 2017, the re-employment age will also be raised to 67.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Under the Adapt and Grow initiative, we are also providing extra career and employment support to older workers, both the rank-and-file workers and professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The Ministry of Manpower will continue to work closely with our tripartite partners to extend support to all local jobseekers as we go through this period of economic transition.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: On the ground, many of us have seen more residents coming forward to the Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS) seeking help, especially for those who are above 40 years old.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If they lose their jobs, it is very hard for them to find a job.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Even if they find a job, usually the pay is very much lower than what they had previously.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: So, there is also this issue about underemployment.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Sometimes, after a while, they have no choice but to take up any employment that they can find.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I mean they are not choosy but, on the other hand, they do have a family to feed.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Our hearts are with them and we want to know how we can help them further.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The other question I want to ask the Minister is regarding the Place and Train and all the placement programmes.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We have written letters to the Workforce Development Agency (WDA) and all the agencies, including e2i, to help them.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: When we send a resident over, that is the success rate?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: How do you track the success rate of e2i as well as WDA in these placement programmes?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: After they have placed the residents, do you continue to follow up to make sure that there is continued employment?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I have also heard from my residents complaining to me that some employers take them in for a while, just to take advantage of the Government's scheme.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Within three months, they say "You are not suitable." The residents are being fired again, and they are back to square one.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We encourage the jobseekers to walk in on their own so that they do not have to sign up with e2i or WSG.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We allow the matching to go on, on its own.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those jobseekers who are unable to secure jobs through such a platform, that is when they will go to see their Members of Parliament or come to WSG or e2i.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What we do is that we track each and every one individually, in terms of when they first contacted us, what kind of services we provide to them, either send them for employability camp or send them for career coaching, skills upgrading or job placement, and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, right now, we have about a few thousand still on our jobseekers' database.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There is one group that we pay special attention to, "the long-term unemployed".

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the whole, the package of Adapt and Grow initiatives which was strengthened last year has worked well and the outcome has been quite encouraging.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As I have mentioned in my reply, successful jobseekers are becoming more inclusive, including the older workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That is not to say that we have done everything we can do.
